pathways.compact_statement: The Guaviare study describes existing dissidents exploiting El Niño dryness for deforestation revenue and negotiating leverage, not climate causing an insurgency.
alternative_explanations: Political negotiations, group fragmentation, commodity incentives, land speculation and enforcement changes also influence behavior.
pathways.uncertainty: Qualitative subregional study using El Niño as a proxy; not attribution of the event to anthropogenic warming or causal identification of armed-group behavior.
recommendations: No structural linkage issue identified; review each cited passage for its specific causal link, alternatives and uncertainty before treating the pathway as verified.

pathways.compact_statement: Insecurity and territorial control restrict environmental response and reforestation in the Guaviare study area, not all Colombian adaptation.
alternative_explanations: Agency budgets, technical capacity, weak state presence and resource shortages also limit response.
pathways.uncertainty: Subregional participant accounts, not a national estimate of conflict blocking all adaptation or a measured resilience effect.
recommendations: Keep the reverse mechanism bounded to the named institution, population and place supported by its cited evidence; do not infer violence from climate vulnerability.
